negative mood regulation expectancy is associated with current depression after controlling rumination, distraction and other coping behaviors.

the relationship between negative mood regulation expectances (NMRE) and current depression was significant even after controlling for rumination, distraction and active coping.

the role of negative mood regulation expectations in the experience of depression.
the relationship of negative mood regulation expectancy (NMRE) with depression, rumination, and distraction.
the effects of negative mood on the cognitive and behavioral functioning of the individual.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
negative mood regulation expectancy is a predictor for depression.

negative mood regulation expectances are associated with both adaptive and maladaptive coping behaviors, and both adaptive and malaptive coping behaviors are associated with depression, but negative mood regulation expectences are more strongly related to depression than either of these coping behaviors.
negative mood regulation expectancy is an important predictor of depression and it is not a result of depression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
negative mood regulation expectances are a better predictor of depression and anxiety than are rumination and distraction.
individuals high in negative mood expectancies have a tendency to engage in maladaptive coping responses.
the relationship between rumination and negative affect is not direct, but rather mediated by negative mood regulation expectencies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
negative mood regulation expectencies have a strong impact on mood.
negative mood regulation expectances are not just a belief that certain behaviors will make you feel better; they are also a belief that these same behaviors will actually work.
the way you think about how you can regulate your mood has a direct effect on the way your mood is actually regulated.
